title: Functional Groups
subject: Chemistry
chapter: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques
objective: Two molecules can share the same carbon chain and still behave differently. How one small group of atoms gives a compound its chemical identity: –OH, –CHO, C=O, –COOH and –NH₂.

fill.q: A functional group is an atom or group of ____ that largely decides a compound's chemical properties.

tf.q: A functional group is always a single atom.
tf.explain: It can be one atom or a group of atoms.

tf.q: An aldehyde and a ketone both contain C=O.
tf.explain: In a ketone, C=O sits between two carbons.

tf.q: Two compounds with the same carbon chain must react the same way.
tf.explain: A different functional group gives different reactions.

tf.q: Chain length can change the boiling point.
tf.explain: The group largely decides chemical behaviour, not every property.

ar.a: Ethanol and propanoic acid react differently with NaHCO₃.
An aldehyde and a ketone are different families.
ar.r: In an aldehyde, C=O is at the end of the chain.

mcq.explain: C=O sits between two carbon atoms.

mcq.q: Which compound is a carboxylic acid?

mcq.explain: N is in the amine group.

num.q: How many carbon atoms are in CH₃CH₂–COOH?
How many oxygen atoms are in the –COOH group?

short.q: Name the family of each: CH₃CH₂–OH, CH₃CH₂–CHO, CH₃CH₂–NH₂.
